reference: GNU Bash runs GNU coreutils tail on the same relative fixture bytes; GNU mkdir -p independently mirrors the nested private runtime-directory creation performed by sv. Metadata is checked as a Bash builtin contract against the documented sv help text.
coverage: Bash type/help metadata identifies sv as a builtin and exposes documented command entries.
sv log matches GNU tail for NUL-containing data, a 4096-byte line, multiple records, and an unterminated final record.
sv log matches GNU tail for -n 0, counts below and above the number of records, empty files, and blank records.
The parity fixtures compare the nested relative BASHSV_RUNDIR tree, created by sv and independently by GNU mkdir -p in the reference run.
exclusions: Service execution and process-control verbs are deferred because this task forbids running service managers or signalling processes; they require an isolated disposable VM with an owned service tree and child-process containment.

Privilege and namespace directives, activation protocols, timers, and readiness/dependency behavior are deferred because they require disposable privilege, process, socket, event, or cron-spool fixtures described with each deferred case.
No absolute service paths, host services, real network peers, user credentials, privileged operations, or system-wide process controls are used.

cases.purpose: Use only Bash's type and help builtins to check the registered builtin kind and documented sv synopsis entries.
cases.script:
kind=$(type -t sv)
[[ $kind == builtin ]] || exit 41
doc=$(help sv)
[[ $doc == *"Service supervisor for bash-os."* ]] || exit 42
[[ $doc == *"sv log NAME [-n N]"* ]] || exit 43
[[ $doc == *"sv shutdown"* ]] || exit 44
printf '%s\n' "$kind"

cases.purpose: Compare sv log's last-four-record output byte-for-byte with GNU tail, including an embedded NUL, a long record, and a final record without LF. GNU mkdir -p mirrors sv's nested private runtime directory so filesystem effects are compared too.
cases.script:
printf 'binary\000record\n' > fixture
line=
printf -v line '%*s' 4096 ''
line=${line// /x}
printf '%s\nmiddle\nlast-without-newline' "$line" >> fixture
export BASHSV_DIR=services BASHSV_RUNDIR=state/deep/run BASHSV_LOGDIR=.
if [[ $(type -t sv) == builtin ]]; then
  sv log fixture -n 4
else
  mkdir -p state/deep/run
  tail -n 4 fixture
fi

cases.purpose: Compare several valid line counts, including zero, one, more than the available records, and a count far above the file length, against GNU tail.
cases.script:
printf 'alpha\nbeta\ngamma\n' > fixture
counts=(0 1 2 4 20)
export BASHSV_DIR=services BASHSV_RUNDIR=state/deep/run BASHSV_LOGDIR=.
if [[ $(type -t sv) == builtin ]]; then
  for n in "${counts[@]}"; do sv log fixture -n "$n"; done
else
  mkdir -p state/deep/run
  for n in "${counts[@]}"; do tail -n "$n" fixture; done
fi

cases.purpose: Check empty-file behavior and preservation of blank LF records at zero, one, two, and excess line counts against GNU tail.
cases.script:
: > empty
printf '\n\n' > blank
counts=(0 1 2 3)
export BASHSV_DIR=services BASHSV_RUNDIR=state/deep/run BASHSV_LOGDIR=.
if [[ $(type -t sv) == builtin ]]; then
  for n in "${counts[@]}"; do sv log empty -n "$n"; done
  for n in "${counts[@]}"; do sv log blank -n "$n"; done
else
  mkdir -p state/deep/run
  for n in "${counts[@]}"; do tail -n "$n" empty; done
  for n in "${counts[@]}"; do tail -n "$n" blank; done
fi

cases.purpose: Qualify once/up/down/restart/signal/status/run and shutdown semantics with services confined to an owned fixture process tree.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r1: No service verb has executed.; r2: Not executed.; r3: Not executed.; r4: Not executed.

cases.purpose: Qualify restart policies, finish hooks, readiness checks, oneshot behavior, and dependency-ordered boot and shutdown.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r1: Not executed.; r3: Notification readiness was recorded; check, COMMAND and timeout readiness branches were not exercised.; r4: Not executed.; r5: Not executed.

cases.purpose: Qualify socket and path activation, notify readiness, and timer scheduling without contacting host services or peers.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r1: Not executed; loopback is authorized in the VM.; r2: Not executed; unprivileged on a private directory.; r4: Not executed; private spool dir via env.

cases.purpose: Qualify service user drops, capability drops, and namespace directives.
cases.reason: Namespace directives (with a user namespace) and directive-failure handling are unprivileged; actual user and capability drops need guest case option to run a side as uid 0 inside a private mount namespace with fixture /etc/passwd and /etc/group bind-mounted (guest.py terminal.child_limits always drops to uid 2000; a drop to a second synthetic uid needs CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID, the legacy runner disables user namespaces, and an unprivileged user namespace maps only one uid).
